# Navimower Map Card 0.3.7-beta8

## Per-zone prepared mowing layers

Use Navimower 0.4.5-beta14's prepared resource API instead of repeatedly transporting the complete mowing footprint for vendor-owned maps.

- Discover the ready-only artifact manifest automatically. Download only changed zone resources; retain unchanged zone elements and decoded images.
- Display backend SVG alpha masks in the original mower-local coordinate frame, with the configured trail color and opacity. Decode replacements before swapping them into existing zone elements.
- Share simultaneous manifest requests and image resources between cards in the same Home Assistant connection, scoped by entry, zone and resource ID. Bound binary downloads to two at a time, and release unused blob URLs.
- Reject previous-cycle responses and remove affected resources on confirmed resets. Geometry revisions are freshness, not cycle identity. Pending builds keep valid same-cycle prefixes visible.
- Support Single and Multi mower views. Keep Multi zone-image DOM stable through live-tail refreshes. Hide cumulative masks for selected History sessions.
- Keep MQTT live-tail semantics, geometric precision, zone editing, underlays, mower controls and schedules unchanged.
- Preserve the legacy composite path for older integrations, unavailable authenticated image transports, and mowers with any MQTT/History fallback zones. This conservative whole-member fallback avoids clipping or double-painting mixed-source geometry. Other fully vendor-owned members can independently use resource mode.
- Add native Chromium regression coverage using the cumulative production runtime, actual SVG image decoding and deterministic synthetic API responses. No user diagnostics or credentials are embedded in tests.

Pair with Navimower **0.4.5-beta14** or newer for per-zone transport. No additional YAML setting is required. Reload the browser/frontend after updating the card.

This remains SVG, not PNG/WebP. Tests verify avoided duplicate requests and unchanged-node reuse; end-user load times, CPU and memory improvements still require field measurement.
